what_its_for: Fenofibric acid is used to lower high levels of triglycerides (fats) in your blood and to raise your good cholesterol (HDL). It may also be used along with a statin medicine to help control your cholesterol levels. Keeping your cholesterol and triglycerides in a healthy range can help protect your heart and blood vessels.
how_to_take: Take fenofibric acid by mouth, with or without food. Swallow the capsule or tablet whole — do not crush, chew, or break it. Try to take it at the same time each day to help you remember. Also follow a heart-healthy, low-fat diet while taking this medicine, as directed by your doctor.
dosing: The usual dose for adults is 35 mg to 105 mg once daily, depending on your condition and your doctor's instructions. Your doctor will start you on the dose that is right for you. Do not change your dose without talking to your doctor first.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — unless it is almost time for your next dose. In that case, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store fenofibric acid at room temperature, between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not use after the expiration date on the label.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking large amounts of alcohol while taking this medicine, as it can raise triglyceride levels and increase the risk of liver problems. Avoid taking antacids that contain magnesium or aluminum within 2 hours of your dose, as they may reduce how well the medicine works. Tell your doctor about all other medicines you take, especially blood thinners like warfarin (Coumadin), other cholesterol medicines, or immunosuppressants like cyclosporine, as dangerous interactions can occur.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away if you experience: unexplained muscle pain, tenderness, weakness, or dark-colored urine (these could be signs of a serious muscle condition called rhabdomyolysis); yellowing of your skin or eyes, stomach pain, or unusual tiredness (possible signs of liver problems); severe stomach pain (possible sign of pancreatitis); allergic reactions such as rash, hives, swelling of your face or throat, or difficulty breathing; or unusual bruising or bleeding if you also take a blood thinner.
when_it_works: You may not feel any different while taking this medicine because high triglycerides and cholesterol usually have no symptoms. Your doctor will check your blood levels after 4 to 8 weeks to see if the medicine is working. It may take a few months to see the full benefit. Keep taking the medicine even if you feel fine — stopping it without your doctor's approval can allow your levels to rise again.
special_populations: Older adults (65 and over): Your doctor may start you on a lower dose and monitor you more closely, as kidney function naturally decreases with age and this medicine is removed by the kidneys. Kidney disease: If you have kidney problems, your doctor will adjust your dose or may decide this medicine is not safe for you. Liver disease: This medicine should NOT be used if you have active liver disease. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Fenofibric acid is generally not recommended during pregnancy or while breastfeeding. Talk to your doctor right away if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding.
